find_networks_near.description: Find the bike share schemes closest to a point, nearest first, each with how far away it is. Use it to answer "is there bike share where I'm going?" before looking for a station. No API key required.
find_networks_near.name: find_networks_near

parameters.description: Latitude of the point to search from, in decimal degrees (48.8566 for Paris).
parameters.name: latitude

parameters.description: Longitude of the point to search from, in decimal degrees (2.3522 for Paris).
parameters.name: longitude

parameters.description: How far from the point to look, in kilometres. 50 by default: a city and its neighbours. Raise it to cover a region.
parameters.name: radius_km

parameters.description: Optional. How many results to return, nearest first. Between 1 and 200; 10 by default.
parameters.name: limit

count.description: How many records are in this page.

latitude.description: The latitude that was searched from.

longitude.description: The longitude that was searched from.

nearest_network.description: The closest network, ready to feed straight into a station lookup. Null when nothing was in range.

city.description: The city it serves, as the operator writes it.

companies.description: The companies running the scheme. Often more than one: an operator plus the firm that makes the docks.

country.description: The country's name, e.g. 'France'. Null for the rare code with no name on file.

country_code.description: The country's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. 'FR'.

source_url.description: Where CityBikes reads this network's data from.

system.description: The platform the scheme runs on, e.g. 'Nextbike'. Networks sharing a system behave alike. Null when it isn't known.

find_stations_near.description: Find the docking stations closest to a point, nearest first, each with how far away it is and what is waiting there. Ask for a minimum number of bikes to find somewhere to pick one up, or a minimum number of free docks to find somewhere to leave one. Leave the network blank and it searches the schemes nearest the point, so a set of coordinates is all you need. No API key required.
find_stations_near.name: find_stations_near

parameters.description: Latitude of the point to search from, in decimal degrees (48.8566 for Paris).
parameters.name: latitude

parameters.description: Longitude of the point to search from, in decimal degrees (2.3522 for Paris).
parameters.name: longitude

parameters.description: How far from the point to look, in kilometres. 1 by default: about a ten-minute walk. Up to 100.
parameters.name: radius_km

parameters.description: Optional. The network to search. Leave blank to search the networks closest to the point, which is what you want when you know where you are but not what the local scheme is called.
parameters.name: network_id

parameters.description: Optional. Only stations with at least this many bikes waiting. Set it to 1 to skip the empty ones. Stations that don't report a bike count are left out, since they can't be shown to meet the minimum.
parameters.name: min_free_bikes

parameters.description: Optional. Only stations with at least this many free docks. Use it to find somewhere to return a bike. Stations that don't report a dock count are left out.
parameters.name: min_empty_slots

parameters.description: Optional. How many nearby networks to open when no network is named: 3 by default, up to 5. Cities often have more than one scheme, so the default looks at a few; each one is a separate request, so keep it low unless you need the overlap. Ignored when a network is chosen.
parameters.name: max_networks

parameters.description: Optional. How many results to return, nearest first. Between 1 and 200; 10 by default.
parameters.name: limit

longitude.description: The longitude that was searched from.

nearest_station.description: The closest station that passed the filters. Null when nothing was in range.

address.description: The street address, for the operators that publish one. Null otherwise.

availability_ratio.description: The share of usable docks holding a bike, 0 to 1. 1 means full of bikes and nowhere to return one; 0 means empty.

distance_km.description: How far the station is from the point that was searched from, in kilometres. Null outside a proximity search.

ebikes.description: Electric bikes among the available ones, for the networks that break the figure down.

empty_slots.description: Docks free to return a bike to. Null when the operator doesn't report it, and always null at a virtual station.

extra.description: Everything the operator reports, exactly as CityBikes passed it on. The keys differ per operator; the named fields above are the ones that recur, already normalised.

free_bikes.description: Bikes available to take right now. Null when the operator doesn't report it, which is not the same as zero.

has_ebikes.description: True when at least one electric bike is waiting here.

has_payment_terminal.description: True when the station has a terminal that takes payment.

id.description: The station's CityBikes id. Get a station takes one of these.

is_empty.description: True when no bike is available here.

is_full.description: True when no dock is free, so a bike can't be returned.

is_online.description: True when the station itself is up. Null for the operators that never report it.

is_renting.description: True when the station is handing bikes out. False during maintenance or out of hours.

is_returning.description: True when the station is accepting returns.

is_virtual.description: True for a station with no physical dock: bikes are left inside a marked area rather than locked to a stand.

last_updated.description: When the operator last refreshed this station, ISO 8601 UTC. Earlier than the timestamp above, which is when CityBikes read it.

longitude.description: Where the station is.

description: Live public bike share data for about 800 schemes worldwide, from Vélib' in Paris to Citi Bike in New York, all through one API. Find the networks near a place, search them by city or operator, and read any station's bikes and free docks right now, including how many of the bikes are electric. Find the stations nearest a set of coordinates without knowing what the local scheme is called, locate dockless bikes and scooters parked loose, and add a whole network up into one availability figure for a scheduled check. No account or API key required.
